# EPEDE 2.0 — COMPREHENSIVE TECHNICAL AUDIT SPECIFICATION & PLATFORM REFERENCE
========================================================================================
Platform Name: EPEDE (Electrical Power Engineering Digital Environment)
Version: 2.0 Enterprise
Lead Engineer & Architect: Mounjouonpou Yaya (Electrical and Power Systems Engineer)
Target Standards: IEC, IEEE, CIGRE, NF C 13-100 / 13-200 / 15-100, Cameroon Grid Code
Canonical Public URL: https://epede-platform.vercel.app
Repository: https://github.com/YAYAMOUNJOUONPOU/epede-platform.git
Core Technology Stack: React 19, TypeScript 5.8, Tailwind CSS, Vite, Three.js, Lucide Icons

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1: PLATFORM OBJECTIVE & ARCHITECTURAL FOUNDATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EPEDE is an authoritative, bilingual (English & French) engineering knowledge environment
created to bridge the gap between abstract academic electrical engineering theory and the
real-world physical infrastructure of electrical power systems.

Product Boundary Definition:
EPEDE is an educational knowledge platform providing interactive worked examples and
physical sensitivity models. It is NOT an engineering sizing tool, protection approval system,
or certification platform, and does not replace certified industrial design software
(ETAP, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, AutoCAD Electrical).

Key Architectural Tenets:
1. Physical Fidelity: Every piece of apparatus, substation bay, transmission tower, and
   protection relay is modeled with authentic electrical specifications, ANSI device numbers,
   and physical construction details.
2. Normative Rigor: Formulations strictly cite international standards (IEC 60909 for
   short-circuits, IEC 60364 for LV installations, IEEE 80-2013 for grounding safety,
   IEEE 519-2022 for harmonics, IEC 62305 for lightning protection).
3. Geographical Grounding: Real-world modeling of the Cameroon National Power Grid,
   including the Southern Interconnected Grid (RIS) and Northern Interconnected Grid (RIN),
   operated by SONATREL and ENEO.
4. Clean Decoupled Frontend: Client-side single-page architecture built with React 19,
   TypeScript 5.8, Tailwind CSS, and Vite, with pre-rendered semantic HTML fallback for
   universal AI agent accessibility.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2: CANONICAL 16 ELECTROTECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE DOMAINS (D01 TO D16)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
D01 — Energy Resources & Generation:
- Hydroelectric dams: Francis, Pelton, and Kaplan hydraulic turbines; water head calculations (H_net), discharge (Q), hydraulic power (P_hyd = rho * g * Q * H * eta).
- Thermal & gas turbine plants: Open-cycle (OCGT) and combined-cycle (CCGT) Brayton-Rankine thermodynamics.
- Solar photovoltaic parks: Irradiance models, MPPT algorithms, string inverters, central inverters.
- Synchronous generators: Stator windings, salient-pole vs cylindrical rotors, automatic voltage regulators (AVR), exciter systems (brushless / static), capability curves (P-Q diagram).

D02 — Power-System Architecture & Grid Planning:
- Network topology: Radial, meshed, and interconnected grid architectures.
- Power flow & dynamic stability: Generation-load balance, N-1 contingency criterion, inertia constant (H), and frequency control reserves (primary, secondary, tertiary).

D03 — Transmission Networks:
- Transmission voltages: 225 kV, 110 kV, 90 kV (No 400 kV network in Cameroon).
- Line parameters: Series resistance (R), inductive reactance (X_L), shunt susceptance (B_C), surge impedance Z_c = sqrt(L/C), Surge Impedance Loading SIL = V^2 / Z_c.
- Infrastructure: Galvanized steel lattice towers (suspension, tension, transposition, terminal), bundled ACSR conductors (Almelec / Aster), composite silicone & porcelain disc insulators, Optical Ground Wire (OPGW).

D04 — Substations & Grid Nodes:
- Air-Insulated Substations (AIS) & Gas-Insulated Substations (GIS) in metal-enclosed SF6 compartments.
- Busbar schemes: Single busbar with sectionalizer, double busbar with bus coupler, 1.5-breaker configuration.
- Primary switchgear: SF6 live-tank circuit breakers (245 kV), vacuum circuit breakers, knee/pantograph disconnectors, fast earthing switches.
- Bay Control Unit (BCU) interlocking logic: Mechanical and electrical interlock sequences preventing on-load disconnector operation or closing earth switches onto energized busbars.

D05 — Distribution Networks (MV/LV):
- Primary distribution: 15 kV (legacy) and 30 kV (standardized) urban underground rings and rural overhead radial feeders.
- Equipment ratings: 15 kV networks utilize 24 kV rated switchgear (U_m = 24 kV); 30 kV networks require 36 kV rated switchgear (U_m = 36 kV) per IEC 62271-200.
- Secondary substations: Ring Main Units (RMU), compact modular switchgear, transformer protection (fused switch disconnector vs vacuum breaker with self-powered relay).
- Distribution transformers: H61 pole-mounted hermetically sealed oil transformers (50 kVA, 100 kVA, 160 kVA), ground-mounted pad-mount transformers (250 kVA - 1600 kVA).
- Low voltage networks: 400 V three-phase / 230 V single-phase, bundled aerial cables (ABC).

D06 — Electrical Installations & Industrial LV:
- Low-voltage distribution: Main Low Voltage Switchboard (TGBT), Form 1 to Form 4b internal separation (IEC 61439-2).
- Earthing regimes (SLT): TT, TN-C, TN-S, and IT systems. Fault current loops (Id), touch voltages (Ud), and automatic disconnection times per IEC 60364-4-41 (ta <= 0.2 s for TT at 230 V; ta <= 0.4 s for TN at 230 V on final circuits).
- Cable sizing & voltage drop per IEC 60364-5-52 Annex G: Conductor current-carrying capacity, derating factors (temperature, grouping, soil), and allowable drop (3% lighting, 5% other).

D07 — Industrial Automation, Drives & Control:
- Motor starting architectures: Direct-On-Line (DOL, current 6-8 x In), Star-Delta (2.5-3 x In), Soft Starter, and Variable Frequency Drive (VFD).
- Power electronics: Inverter DC bus, PWM modulation, dV/dt output filters, and bearing current mitigation.
- Process control: PLC architecture (IEC 61131-3), P&ID reading per ISA-5.1, 4-20 mA current loops, and HART communication.

D08 — Extra-Low Voltage & Special Systems (ELV/CFA):
- Structured cabling: Category 6A / 7 copper and single-mode fiber-optic distribution.
- Security & safety: IP CCTV surveillance, biometric access control, fire detection systems, and clean-agent extinguishing (FM200 / Novec).

D09 — Advanced Technologies, AI & Digital Twin:
- Digital twins of substation assets, IIoT condition monitoring, vibration analysis, and operational technology (OT) cybersecurity boundaries.

D10 — Energy Storage & EV Infrastructure:
- Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS): Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) chemistry, bidirectional Power Conversion Systems (PCS), frequency response, and peak shaving.
- EV charging infrastructure: AC Level 2 destination chargers and DC fast chargers (CCS2 / CHAdeMO).

D11 — Protection Relaying, Measurement & Fault Studies:
- ANSI protective functions: 50/51 overcurrent, 50N/51N neutral overcurrent, 67/67N directional, 21 distance (mho/quadrilateral), 87T/87L differential with harmonic restraint, 50BF breaker failure.
- Instrument transformers: CT secondary wiring (Ohm's law: changing 5A to 1A reduces I^2*R cable losses by 25 times and voltage drop IR by 5 times for equal burden resistance).
- Short-circuit calculations per IEC 60909-0:2016: Initial symmetrical current Ik'', peak current ip = kappa * sqrt(2) * Ik'', breaking current Ib, thermal equivalent current Ith.

D12 — Substation Automation Systems (SAS) & Telecontrol:
- IEC 61850 substation bus (MMS, GOOSE peer-to-peer tripping) and process bus (Sampled Values SV per IEC 61850-9-2LE).
- Precision Time Protocol: IEEE 1588v2 PTP for microsecond synchronization of merging units and protection IEDs.

D13 — Operational Communications & OT Networks:
- Industrial Ethernet switches, teleprotection signaling, SCADA protocols (IEC 60870-5-104, DNP3, Modbus TCP), and OPGW optical transmission.

D14 — Power Quality & Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC):
- Waveform distortion: Total Harmonic Distortion (THD_V < 8% for <= 1 kV per IEEE 519-2022 Table 1; THD_V < 5% for 1 kV to 69 kV).
- Power quality events: Voltage sags, swells, transients, flicker (Pst, Plt per IEC 61000-4-15), unbalance factor, passive tuned LC filters, and active harmonic filters.

D15 — Smart Metering & Grid Digitalization:
- Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), smart meters, DLMS/COSEM communication protocols, cellular/PLC backhaul, anti-fraud algorithms, and STS prepaid tokens.

D16 — Earthing Systems, Lightning & Electrical Safety:
- Substation grounding safety per IEEE 80-2013: Mesh earthing grid design with copper conductors and rods; safety evaluated strictly by mesh voltage Em <= Etouch and step voltage Es <= Estep (not by a generic Rg <= 1 Ohm rule).
- Lightning protection: Rolling sphere method, mesh method, and protection angle per IEC 62305; metal-oxide surge arresters (ZnO) per IEC 60099-4.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3: CAMEROON NATIONAL POWER GRID TOPOLOGY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Southern Interconnected Grid (RIS - Réseau Interconnecté Sud):
- Major Hydro Generation Centers:
  * Song Loulou Hydro Dam: 384 MW (8 x 48 MW Francis turbines), located on the Sanaga river; primary frequency-regulating station of the RIS.
  * Nachtigal Hydro Plant: 420 MW (7 x 60 MW Francis turbines), Cameroon's newest baseload hydro generation asset.
  * Edéa Hydro Facility: 276 MW (mix of Francis and Kaplan units on the Sanaga river).
  * Memve’ele Hydro Plant: 211 MW (4 x 52.75 MW Francis units on the Ntem river), evacuated via 225 kV line Nyabizan -> Ebolowa -> Ahala (Yaoundé) (~280 km).
  * Lom Pangar Reservoir Dam: 6 billion m³ regulating reservoir holding Sanaga flow at ~1,000 m³/s during the dry season.
- Thermal Gas & Heavy Fuel Generation:
  * Kribi Gas Power Plant: 216 MW (Wärtsilä 18V50DF engines fired with offshore natural gas from Sanaga South).
  * Dibamba Heavy Fuel Oil Plant: 88 MW (Wärtsilä engines for peak shaving).
- Primary Transmission Backbone (SONATREL):
  * 225 kV Line: Song Loulou - Mangombe - Oyomabang (supplying Yaoundé).
  * 225 kV Line: Song Loulou - Bekoko (supplying Douala).
  * 225 kV Line: Nachtigal - Nyom II (Yaoundé injection).
  * 225 kV Line: Nachtigal - Wouro Soua (RIS-RIN interconnection tie, under construction / PIRECT project).
  * 90 kV Regional sub-transmission loops around Douala (Bekoko, Logbaba, Koumassi, Deido) and Yaoundé (Oyomabang, Kondengui, Ahala, Nyom II).

Northern Interconnected Grid (RIN - Réseau Interconnecté Nord):
- Generation: Lagdo Hydro Dam (72 MW, 4 x 18 MW units on the Benue River) supplemented by emergency thermal capacity.
- Transmission: 110 kV and 90 kV lines connecting Garoua, Maroua, Guider, and Ngaoundéré.
- Interconnection Project (RIS-RIN): High-voltage 225 kV link (530 km from Nachtigal to Wouro Soua with new substations at Ntui, Yoko, Tibati, Wouro Soua) under construction under the World Bank / MINEE PIRECT project.
